newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIA's SilkAir in B737-300 sale, leaseback.
newsitem.headline: SIA's SilkAir in B737-300 sale, leaseback.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd's (SIA) regional airline SilkAir said on Tuesday it has signed a sale and leaseback agreement with General Electric Capital Aviation Services (GECAS) for two of its four owned B737-300 aircraft.
GECAS, a unit of General Electric, is a major aircraft leasing company.
A SilkAir statement gave no financial details but said it was able to take advantage of the present strong market values of the B737-300.
The aircraft will be leased back to SilkAir for two years with an option for extension, the statement said.
SilkAir also said it is currently reviewing its future fleet requirements, and studying the Boeing B737-600/700/800 family of aircraft, the Airbus A320/319 and the McDonnell Douglas MD90/95.

SilkAir is reviewing the aircraft as possible replacements for its present fleet of five B737-300s (one leased) and two leased Fokker F70 aircraft, the statement said. A decision will be made in early 1997.
SilkAir recently signed a three-year operating lease agreement with GECAS for a sixth B737-300 aircraft which will be delivered in March 1997. -- Singapore newsroom 65-8703080
